title: 「X is more of A than B」與其說 X 是 B，不如說 X 是 A
titleZh: 「X is more of A than B」與其說 X 是 B，不如說 X 是 A
titleEn: Using “X is more of A than B”

formula: Subject + be + more of + noun phrase A + than + noun phrase B

formulas.formula: Subject + be + more of + noun phrase A + than + noun phrase B

example: The disagreement is more of a communication problem than a technical one.
exampleZh: 這次分歧與其說是技術問題，不如說是溝通問題。

examples.en: The disagreement is more of a communication problem than a technical one.
examples.zh: 這次分歧與其說是技術問題，不如說是溝通問題。
examples.highlight: The disagreement is more of a communication problem than a technical one.

rules.zh: 在【X is more of A than B】中，A 是說話者認為較準確的描述。例句【The meeting was more of an introduction than a negotiation.】中，較準確的描述是【an introduction】，較不準確的描述是【a negotiation】。把 A 和 B 的位置對調，句子意思也會改變。
rules.en: In X is more of A than B, A is the stronger or more accurate description. For example, in ‘The meeting was more of an introduction than a negotiation’, an introduction is the more accurate description and a negotiation is the less accurate one. Reversing A and B changes the meaning.

rules.zh: 詞語【more of】和 than 後通常使用名詞或名詞組。直接比較形容詞時，應使用另一個句型，而不是本課的 more of A than B。
rules.en: Use noun phrases after “more of” and “than” The words after more of and than are normally nouns or noun phrases. The task was more of a test than a game. The speech was more of an appeal than a policy statement. The task was more of difficult than enjoyable. For a direct adjective comparison, use a different structure: The task was more difficult than enjoyable.

rules.zh: 在 more of A than B 中，A 和 B 若是單數可數名詞，通常都要各自使用 a 或 an。輔音讀音前用 a，例如 a warning；元音讀音前用 an，例如 an opportunity。冠詞取決於讀音，不只看拼寫。
rules.en: Use “a” or “an” with singular countable nouns The event was more of a celebration than a ceremony. The delay was more of an inconvenience than a disaster. Use a before a consonant sound: a warning a lesson a technical problem Use an before a vowel sound: an opportunity an inconvenience an emotional reaction

rules.zh: 詞語【warning】和 request 都是單數可數名詞，因此兩者前面都需要冠詞。
rules.en: Repeat the article when necessary The message was more of a warning than a request. The message was more of a warning than request.

rules.zh: 如果 A 和 B 使用相同的中心名詞，可以用 one 代替第二次出現的單數名詞。只有在讀者能清楚知道 one 代替哪個名詞時，才應使用這種寫法。
rules.en: Use “one” to avoid repeating the same noun The disagreement is more of a communication problem than a technical problem. This is grammatically correct, but the repeated noun can be replaced with one: The disagreement is more of a communication problem than a technical one. Other examples: a timing issue → a money one a cosmetic problem → a structural one a personal decision → a political one However, use one only when the missing noun is clear.

rules.zh: 在 more of A than B 後若是不可以數或抽象名詞，通常不需要冠詞。例句中的 training和 proof 都按不可數用法處理，因此可寫 full training 和 firm proof；不可機械地在所有 A、B 前加入 a 或 an。
rules.en: Uncountable nouns do not always need an article The programme was more of a short introduction than full training. The early result was more of an indication than firm proof. training and proof are uncountable in these examples, so they do not require a or an.

rules.zh: 句中的 be 或 become 必須保留原句的時態和語氣：現在用 is，過去用 was，現在完成可用 has become，過去完成可用 had become，表達可能性則可用 could be。more of A than B 的比較部分保持不變。
rules.en: Preserve the correct form of “be” Present: The book is more of a guide than a textbook. Past: The meeting was more of an introduction than a negotiation. Present perfect: The app has become more of a social platform than a messaging tool. Past perfect: The weekly meeting had become more of a progress check than a decision-making session. Modal: The policy could be more of a public-relations exercise than an environmental measure.

rules.zh: 這句比較水和果汁的數量，並不是把一件事歸類為 A 而不是 B。這句比較兩種描述，表示「警告」比「請求」更能準確形容這次討論。
rules.en: Do not confuse classification with quantity The bottle contains more water than juice. This compares quantities. It does not use the target structure. The discussion was more of a warning than a request. This compares two possible descriptions of the discussion.

rules.zh: 這句不一定表示活動完全沒有正式元素，而是表示整體而言，「慶祝活動」是更準確的描述。
rules.en: The sentence does not completely deny B The event was more of a celebration than a formal ceremony. This does not necessarily mean that the event contained no formal elements. It means that celebration is the better overall description.

rules.zh: 副詞 really、actually、perhaps、probably、clearly 等可以加入句中，用來表達態度或確定程度，但它們不是固定結構的一部分；核心仍是 more of A than B。
rules.en: Optional words must not be treated as part of the fixed structure Words such as the following may be added: really actually perhaps probably clearly The speech was perhaps more of an appeal than a policy statement. The article was actually more of an opinion piece than an objective report. These words add attitude or certainty, but the core structure remains: more of A than B

benefits.zh: 有時一個人、事件或情況同時帶有 A 和 B 的特徵。這個句型讓你指出哪一個描述較為準確。這次面試與其說是正式評估，不如說是友善交談。 面試可能仍然包含評估成分，但整體感覺更接近友善交談。
benefits.en: It helps you choose between two possible descriptions Sometimes a person, event or situation has features of both A and This structure lets you show which description is more accurate. The interview was more of a friendly conversation than a formal assessment. The interview may still have included some assessment, but its overall character was closer to a conversation.

benefits.zh: 第一個版本完全否定「談判」這個描述。第二個版本較有分寸：它容許兩種描述都有部分道理，但清楚指出哪一種更準確。
benefits.en: It avoids making an overly absolute statement Compare: The meeting was not a negotiation. It was an introduction. The meeting was more of an introduction than a negotiation. The first version completely rejects the idea of a negotiation. The second version is more balanced: it accepts that both descriptions may contain some truth, while showing that one is more accurate.

benefits.zh: 使用這個句型，可以把兩項相關判斷合併成一句，不需要重複主語或另外使用 however。
benefits.en: It combines two judgements in one sentence Without this structure: The book is useful as a guide. However, it is not really a textbook. With this structure: The book is more of a guide than a textbook.

benefits.zh: 和 difficult 等形容詞有時過於籠統。這個句型讓你更準確地說明某件事究竟屬於哪一類。第二句清楚說明了會議的實際功能。
benefits.en: It makes evaluations more precise Words such as good, bad, useful and difficult can be too general. The structure allows you to explain exactly what kind of thing something is. good, bad, useful General: The meeting was useful. More precise: The meeting was more of a progress check than a decision-making session.

benefits.zh: 與其直接說對方「錯了」，你可以用這個句型提出較準確的理解。這種表達在會議、討論和專業溝通中通常較有分寸。
benefits.en: It is useful for polite disagreement and correction Instead of saying: You are wrong. This is not a technical problem. you can say: This is more of a communication problem than a technical one. The second version corrects the description without making the disagreement unnecessarily aggressive.

benefits.zh: 這個句型適合用於討論、報告、評論、簡報和分析文章，因為它能顯示你不是只作簡單判斷，而是在比較不同解釋。
benefits.en: It is useful in discussions, reports and analytical writing You can use this structure to evaluate: a problem a decision a meeting a policy a piece of writing an event a person’s reaction the purpose of an activity.
